title: Agentic Turtles High-Stakes Confirmation Record
description: Attributable external sign-off for one high-stakes plan step, committed at confirmations/<workload>/<step-id>.json on the default branch. Its existence is what unblocks the build, even on an approved, frozen plan (FR-023, FR-024, SC-006). The record is BOUND to the work it was given about: the workload it belongs to, and a digest of the step's own content (amended 2026-08-17, GHI #95) — an authority's answer authorizes THAT step in THAT workload and nothing else.

step_id.description: The plan step this confirms; must equal the <step-id> in the filename (the record is looked up by it)

workload.description: The workload slug this confirms a step of; must equal the <workload> directory in the path. Step ids are unique only WITHIN a plan, so without this two workloads that both declare step-billing-cycle would share one record and one authority's answer would unblock the other's build (GHI #95).

step_digest.description: sha256 over the step's id, intent, acceptance and authority, canonically serialized. B5 recomputes it from the frozen plan and refuses a mismatch, so a re-approval that CHANGED this step invalidates the sign-off while a re-approval that left it alone does not (GHI #95). Obtain it from the review page's high-stakes panel — it prints the record to commit with this field filled in.

authority.description: Must equal the step's authority (FR-023 names the route, FR-024 makes it binding). Extensible in future schema versions.

confirmed_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 instant, zone included — either a Z suffix or a numeric offset. The confirmation is expected AFTER the plan is frozen (FR-024), so the moment is part of the record.

scope.description: The guardrails actually confirmed, in the authority's terms. Must carry non-whitespace text: a blank scope confirms nothing while still unblocking the build.

Confirmer.description: Named person/org + contact context — both halves are what make the record attributable
